instruction: Use speedtest.net to benchmark my internet connection. After the speed test finishes, copy all the measurement results displayed on speedtest.net/results and save them into ~/Test/Speed/results.txt (ensure the directory exists, creating it if necessary). Each metric must be on a separate line with format: metric_name value (separated by one space).

metadata.explanation: Task requires performing an internet speed benchmark using speedtest.net, collecting results from speedtest.net/results, and writing to a text file. Evaluator checks for the presence of three essential metrics: Ping, Download, and Upload. This is a paraphrase of the original instruction.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete format verification: Instruction requires specific format 'metric_name value' with one space separation and each metric on separate line, but file_contains only checks if strings 'Ping', 'Download', 'Upload' exist anywhere in file
No structural validation: Evaluator cannot verify that each metric is on a separate line or that actual measurement values are present (not just metric names)

Insufficient coverage: Instruction says 'copy ALL measurement results', but evaluator only checks for 3 specific metrics (speedtest.net typically displays more information like server, jitter, latency details)
False positive risk: File containing 'Ping Download Upload' as plain text anywhere (without proper formatting or values) would pass evaluation but fail instruction requirements
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use check_list metric with regex patterns to verify each metric appears on separate line with format: '^Ping \d+' '^Download [\d.]+' '^Upload [\d.]+' to ensure proper formatting and presence of numeric values
Consider using more specific patterns like '^Ping \d+(\.\d+)?\s*(ms|milliseconds)?$' to validate both metric name, value, and optional unit on each line
If 'all results' is required, expand expected patterns to include other common speedtest metrics or document that only these 3 core metrics are verified
Alternative: Use a custom getter to parse the file line-by-line and extract metric:value pairs, then use check_direct_json_object to verify structured data
